findings.title: No re-check of cache after acquiring write lock (thundering herd)
findings.body: After the RLock check misses, every concurrent caller takes the write lock in turn and re-reads and parses the manifest from disk (and from the CDN if enabled). The cache is not re-checked once the write lock is held. On startup, or any time the cache is nil, N concurrent requests each do the full file read and JSON decode serially. Add a second check of `entryPointAssetsCache != nil && cfg.Env != setting.Dev` after `Lock()`.

findings.title: Cache overwritten with nil result when loading fails
findings.body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` runs even when `err != nil`, so `result` is nil. A transient failure, for example a missing manifest, replaces a previously valid cache with nil. In non-dev mode this discards good assets and forces a reload on every call. Callers get `(nil, err)`. The cache should only be updated when `err == nil`. The fix to the data race did not address this.

findings.title: No test covering the race fix
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race but adds no test, such as a concurrent `GetWebAssets` run under `-race`, to guard against regression. Nothing exercises the new locking.
